pr_title: pwm_mcux_sctimer: Add support to change channel period
pr_body:
I had issues changing the PWM period using the ``nxp,sctimer-pwm`` driver. I'm not sure if that would be a valid or an acceptable fix but I hope this would describe my problem well and would serve as a base for further discussion.

Please see a more detailed explanation of the issue commit message:
```txt
    pwm_mcux_sctimer: Add support to change channel period
    
    The NXP HAL creates a new event handle each time the period is changed.
    Changing the period result in a misbehaving PWM since more events are
    configured for the same channel. Moreover, this fails when reaching the
    maximum amount of PWM event.
    
    With the current HAL abstraction, it is not possible to reuse the last
    event handle or remove a registered handle.
    
    When a channel was already configured, we reinitialize the device using
    the HAL and reconfigure all the channels to make sure that every channel
    is using a single event.
    
    For more detail on the root cause if the issue, see the HAL
    implementation or more precisely, the ``s_currentEvent`` variable:
    https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/hal_nxp/blob/master/mcux/mcux-sdk/drivers/sctimer/fsl_sctimer.c#L481
```
Thanks for your feedbacks!

Fixes #https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/58927

issue_context.title: NXP HAL doens't allow changing the PWM period for SCTimer
issue_context.body:
The NXP ``SCTimer`` HAL holds an variable (``s_currentEvent``) which is incremented in the ``SCTimer_CreateAndScheduleEvent`` function. When changing the period on the same channel, ``s_currentEvent`` is incremented again that results in a misbehaving PWM since more events are configured for the same channel.

For more detail of the root cause, please see the HAL implementation:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/hal_nxp/blob/master/mcux/mcux-sdk/drivers/sctimer/fsl_sctimer.c#L481

**Target CPU**: NXP LPC55S36
**Driver**: ``nxp,sctimer-pwm``
